paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea of Hebrews 13: a life that's looking toward the city to come gets REAL practical down here. The writer says, "here we do not have a permanent city, but we are looking for the city that is to come" (Hebrews 13:14). So love the brothers, welcome strangers, remember those in prison, and honor marriage (Hebrews 13:1-4). Nobody packs for a trip and then lives like they're staying forever, and I know that better than most.

So what keeps a baker steady while the road gets bumpy? Two things, and both are Jesus. God has said, "Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you," so we can be content instead of chasing more (Hebrews 13:5). And "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever" (Hebrews 13:8). Strange teachings come and go, but grace is what strengthens the heart (Hebrews 13:9), and Jesus suffered outside the city gate to sanctify the people by His own blood (Hebrews 13:12).

That's why the writer says the response is a life poured out for Him. We go to Jesus, we continually offer "a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name," and we do good and share with others, because with such sacrifices God is pleased (Hebrews 13:15-16). Then he ends the way every good letter should, with the God of peace equipping us "with every good thing to do His will" (Hebrews 13:21), and then "Grace be with all of you" (Hebrews 13:25). So, baker, let's get after it, because grace started this and grace is going to finish it.
